title: Table 2.1. Comparison of hsCRP between simple and complicated appendicitis
objective: determine the diagnostic value of hsCRP in simple acute appendicitis and complicated appendicitis

rows: Mann–Whitney U, two-sided asymptotic tie correction and continuity correction · sensitivity comparison
result.methods: Rank comparison selected conservatively for either n<10 or |skewness|>1; otherwise Welch. Both comparisons retained with distinct estimands.
notes: Histology 1–5 reference-positive; code 6 negative under isolated reactive lymphoid hyperplasia assumption.
Histological severity 1–3 simple, 4–5 complicated; code 6 not applicable. Operative rupture remains independent.
All supplied records retained; full clinical eligibility remains unverified. Missing and unrecognised codes are not negative.
Unit: mg/L. Included 30; excluded not applicable/missing/invalid 6.

Retained reporting convention α = 0.05. P-values are displayed to three decimals, or <0.001 when justified by the calculated value; unrounded inferential values remain in the calculation log where available. Statistical evidence alone does not establish clinical importance. Multiplicity treatment is stated in the methods; unadjusted exploratory comparisons require cautious interpretation.
Complicated: n=12; mean (SD) 15.250 (10.635); median (Q1–Q3) 14.500 (8.500–21.250); observed range 1.000–31.000. Units are those of the measured variable in the title/source notes.
Simple: n=18; mean (SD) 16.000 (9.923); median (Q1–Q3) 16.000 (7.000–25.000); observed range 1.000–31.000. Units are those of the measured variable in the title/source notes.

The retained primary/sensitivity label uses sample size and skewness as a heuristic; it does not establish independence, distributional assumptions or protocol approval. Test choice/prespecification remains a methodological review item. Rank-biserial intervals are percentile bootstrap; the mean-difference interval is Welch-based; the median-difference interval is percentile bootstrap.
result.interpretation: These results address the relationship between histological severity and hsCRP. For complicated minus simple, rank-biserial effect -0.023 (95% interval -0.454 to 0.412); Mann–Whitney (sensitivity comparison) p = 0.932. The unadjusted rank test does not provide evidence of a distributional difference at the 5% level; this does not establish equivalence. The retained primary exploratory Welch comparison estimates a mean difference of -0.750 (95% interval -8.743 to 7.243), t=-0.194, df=22.557, p = 0.848. This does not meet the retained 5% criterion and does not establish equivalence. Mann–Whitney compares distributions and is not automatically a median test. The estimated group difference is associative.
